$comment: Conformance vectors for the bounded-scan range algebra.
The same ScanOpts is evaluated on both sides of the vsock boundary: a
current proxy computes the range itself (enclave-proxy's scan_bounds),
while against an older one the enclave reads the whole prefix and
computes it locally (vti_common::store::scan_bounds). A caller must get
the same rows either way, so the two implementations -- which live in
separate cargo workspaces and cannot share code without coupling them --
are pinned to this one table instead.
Every consumer runs these through its *real* path, not a reimplementation:
- vti-common  the vsock fake parent          (what the client tests run on)
- enclave-proxy  handle_scan                 (fjall range on the parent)
Add a case here before fixing a bounds bug anywhere, so the fix is
proven in every implementation rather than the one that reported it.
Case fields: `keys` are seeded in the keyspace; `expect` is the exact
ordered result of scanning with `prefix`/`after`/`reverse` and no limit.
`encoding` is "utf8" (default) or "hex", the latter for keys that are

cases.name: a prefix scan excludes neighbours on both sides
reverse yields the same rows newest first
descending after is exclusive and walks older
an after equal to the first key yields the rest
an after equal to the prefix itself keeps every row
an ascending after below the prefix does not widen the scan
a descending after above the prefix does not widen the scan
an ascending after past the prefix end yields nothing
a descending after below the prefix start yields nothing
an empty prefix covers the whole keyspace ascending
an empty prefix with an after still resumes exclusively
a prefix with no rows yields nothing
a prefix that is a prefix of another prefix does not leak into it

cases.$comment: 0xFF has no incrementable byte, so the prefix has no upper bound to compute and the scan must simply run to the end of the keyspace.
cases.name: an all-0xFF prefix has no upper bound

cases.$comment: The byte before the boundary must stay out and the boundary itself must come in, which is where an off-by-one in the upper bound shows up.
cases.name: a prefix ending in 0xFF increments the byte before it
a reverse scan over a single row returns it
